_comment: What the dashboard does with each piece of the gateway's user-facing API (docs/api-coverage.md is made from this file).
rpcs: every RPC a signed-in person may call at `release`. fields: every field of every message a client can send.
sdk / bff: whether the Go SDK and the BFF carry it. ui: how a person reaches it in the UI:
form       a dedicated input, select, switch or checkbox
action     a button or a flow runs it
document   only by writing YAML or JSON in an editor, or choosing a file
read-only  shown, cannot be set or called
fixed      the dashboard always sends one value
plumbing   not a person's to author: the workspace of the route, page tokens, concurrency and idempotency tokens
none       the dashboard cannot send it or call it
where: the one place to look, path:line from the repository root. note: one sentence, only when something is partial or wrong.
Edit this file when a feature lands or a gap closes, then run:
python3 deploy/ci/upstream/follow.py api-coverage --write        # rewrite the tables in docs/api-coverage.md
python3 deploy/ci/upstream/follow.py api-coverage --upstream     # is anything of the pinned release unclassified?
The Follow upstream workflow reads it to say, of each thing a new release adds, whether the dashboard has it.

groups.title: Provider profiles
groups.about: A profile's `endpoints` are `NetworkEndpoint` messages, the same as a policy's. Their rows under Policy describe the sandbox policy editors; what the Create profile form can set of an endpoint is in the section on that form above.

groups.title: Policy, settings and proposals
groups.about: The `NetworkEndpoint` rows describe the sandbox policy editors: the rule view (add an endpoint, add a rule, remove) and the document editor.
